slides.title: Test Case Functional Functional Tests represent the first step in guaranteeing software quality, because they allow us t
slides.body:
Test CaseFunctional
because they allow us to verify not only that the application functions as
expected on the technological front but, above all, that it does what users
actually expect with respect to their initial requests.
Functional tests, in fact, take into account the needs of users, give
developers the certainty that business processes meet these needs and
allow Qa (Quality Assurance) teams to verify that the software is actually
ready for release in production.

slides.title: Test Case - Where to start - 1 - Functional To get to the writing of a functional test case we start from the analysis o
slides.body:
Test Case - Where to start -1-Functional
To get to the writing of a functional test case we start from the analysis of
a VF, from which we extract all the possible cases of operation,
converting everything into test case.
Possible test cases can be extracted from descriptive text, from a
descriptive table, from a truth table, from a logical equation, from a state
machine, from a flowchart.

Test Case - Where to start - 8 - Functional In all cases, except for the case of the descriptive text, the process is si
slides.body:
Test Case - Where to start -8-Functional
simpler and more straightforward, because what is written must be
followed and there is not much margin of imagination to be able to
extract some tests. This is because you can not change a truth table
or a flowchart, so just follow what is written and put it in the form of
tests, using the syntax and form chosen for writing the tests
themselves.

slides.title: Test Case Diagnostic The rules relating to the functional safety of electronically managed machines and systems identify
slides.body:
machines and systems identify a particular type of test; diagnostic tests,
which are intended to detect any faults in the electronic components. The
timely detection of faults, especially if they are dangerous, is essential to
keep the system or the machine in a safe state, even in the face of serious
anomalies; in fact, the level of safety integrity (SIL) strongly depends on the
degree of diagnostic coverage and the fraction of dangerous failures
detected.
In this regard, diagnostic test cases are useful to search for malfunctions
("fault") when these happen and take actions to minimize damage first that
the actual failure occurs ("failure").

slides.body:

analysis of a VF, from which we extract all the possible diagnosis
cases, converting everything into test case.
Possible test cases can be extracted from dedicated section in the
VF (if present) and from more detailed diagnostic documents called
CDD.
